title.en: Word types II: the small words

summary.en: Articles, prepositions, conjunctions, numbers, particles, and a method to identify any word.
summary.bs: Članovi, prijedlozi, veznici, brojevi, rječce i metod da prepoznaš bilo koju riječ.

concepts.youtubeQuery: German articles der die das ein eine explained

en.one: The Artikel stands before a noun and shows its gender, number and case. Definite: der, die, das (the). Indefinite: ein, eine (a).
en.explain: der = masculine, die = feminine, das = neuter, and die for all plurals. The article changes with the case: der Mann (subject), den Mann (object), dem Mann (to the man). That's why the article is your best tool for spotting the case.
en.example: 'Ein Hund spielt im Garten. Der Hund ist braun.' First mention: ein; then: der.
en.why: Learn every noun with its article. 'Tisch' alone is useless; 'der Tisch' tells you how to use it.
en.mixup: There's no indefinite article in the plural: 'ein Buch', but 'Bücher' (books), not 'eine Bücher'.

bs.one: Artikel je član: stoji ispred imenice i pokazuje rod, broj i padež. Određeni: der, die, das. Neodređeni: ein, eine.
bs.explain: der = muški rod, die = ženski, das = srednji, i die za svu množinu. Član se mijenja po padežu: der Mann (subjekat), den Mann (objekat), dem Mann (muškarcu). Zato je član tvoj najbolji alat da prepoznaš padež.
bs.example: 'Ein Hund spielt im Garten. Der Hund ist braun.' Prvi put: ein; poslije: der.
bs.why: Uči svaku imenicu s članom. Samo 'Tisch' ne pomaže; 'der Tisch' ti kaže kako je koristiti.
bs.mixup: U množini nema neodređenog člana: 'ein Buch', ali 'Bücher' (knjige), ne 'eine Bücher'.

en.one: A Präposition is a small word before a noun that shows place, time or relation: in, auf, mit, für, nach, von, zu.
en.explain: How to spot it: it is followed by a noun or pronoun group (mit dem Bus, für mich). The big German rule: every preposition decides the case of the noun after it. 'mit' always takes the dative, 'für' always takes the accusative.
en.example: 'Ich fahre mit dem Bus zur Arbeit.' mit and zu are prepositions; zur = zu + der.
en.why: Prepositions are one of the main ways you meet cases in real sentences.
en.mixup: Prepositions often merge with the article: in + dem = im, zu + der = zur, an + das = ans.

bs.one: Präposition je prijedlog: kratka riječ ispred imenice koja pokazuje mjesto, vrijeme ili odnos: in, auf, mit, für, nach, von, zu.
bs.explain: Kako ga prepoznati: iza njega dolazi imenica ili zamjenica (mit dem Bus, für mich). Veliko njemačko pravilo: svaki prijedlog određuje padež imenice iza sebe, isto kao u bosanskom ('s + instrumental', 'bez + genitiv'). 'mit' uvijek traži dativ, 'für' akuzativ.
bs.example: 'Ich fahre mit dem Bus zur Arbeit.' mit i zu su prijedlozi; zur = zu + der.
bs.why: Prijedlozi su jedan od glavnih načina kako ćeš sretati padeže u stvarnim rečenicama.
bs.mixup: Prijedlozi se često stapaju s članom: in + dem = im, zu + der = zur, an + das = ans.

concepts.youtubeQuery: German conjunctions und aber denn weil dass

en.one: A Konjunktion links words or clauses: und, aber, oder, denn, weil, dass, wenn.
en.explain: There are two kinds, and they change word order differently. 'und, aber, oder, denn, sondern' just connect; the word order stays normal. 'weil, dass, wenn, ob, obwohl' start a subordinate clause and push the verb to the very end.
en.example: 'Ich bleibe zu Hause, denn ich bin krank.' vs. 'Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.' Same meaning, different verb position.
en.why: Conjunctions are the gateway to longer sentences, and to the verb-at-the-end rule.
en.mixup: 'denn' and 'weil' both mean 'because', but only 'weil' sends the verb to the end.

bs.one: Konjunktion je veznik: spaja riječi ili rečenice: und, aber, oder, denn, weil, dass, wenn.
bs.explain: Postoje dvije vrste i različito mijenjaju red riječi. 'und, aber, oder, denn, sondern' samo spajaju; red riječi ostaje normalan. 'weil, dass, wenn, ob, obwohl' počinju zavisnu rečenicu i guraju glagol na sam kraj.
bs.example: 'Ich bleibe zu Hause, denn ich bin krank.' i 'Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.' Isto značenje, drugo mjesto glagola.
bs.why: Veznici su ulaz u duže rečenice i u pravilo 'glagol na kraj'.
bs.mixup: 'denn' i 'weil' znače 'jer', ali samo 'weil' šalje glagol na kraj.

en.one: Zahlwörter (Numerale) are number words: eins, zwei, drei (cardinal) and erste, zweite, dritte (ordinal).
en.explain: Numbers 21 to 99 are said 'backwards': 21 = einundzwanzig (one-and-twenty). Ordinals add -te up to 19 (der vierte) and -ste from 20 (der zwanzigste), with exceptions: erste, dritte, siebte. Dates use ordinals: am dritten Mai.
en.example: 'Ich bin vierunddreißig Jahre alt und wohne im zweiten Stock.'
en.why: Prices, times, ages, phone numbers and dates all need numbers, and the backwards order trips up everyone at first.
en.mixup: Write numbers as one word: 'vierunddreißig', never 'vier und dreißig'.

bs.one: Zahlwörter (Numerale) su brojevi: eins, zwei, drei (glavni) i erste, zweite, dritte (redni).
bs.explain: Brojevi od 21 do 99 se govore 'unazad': 21 = einundzwanzig (jedan-i-dvadeset). Redni brojevi dobijaju -te do 19 (der vierte) i -ste od 20 (der zwanzigste), s izuzecima: erste, dritte, siebte. Datumi koriste redne: am dritten Mai.
bs.example: 'Ich bin vierunddreißig Jahre alt und wohne im zweiten Stock.'
bs.why: Cijene, sati, godine, telefoni i datumi trebaju brojeve, a obrnuti red u početku zbuni svakoga.
bs.mixup: Brojeve piši kao jednu riječ: 'vierunddreißig', nikad 'vier und dreißig'.

concepts.youtubeQuery: German modal particles doch mal ja

en.one: Partikeln are small words that add tone, not content: doch, mal, ja, denn, eben. Interjektionen are exclamations: ach, oh, au, na ja.
en.explain: Particles never change form and can't start a sentence. They make German sound natural and polite. 'Komm mal her' is softer than 'Komm her'. 'Doch' also answers a negative question with 'yes': 'Kommst du nicht?' – 'Doch!'.
en.example: 'Das ist ja interessant!' (oh, that's interesting!) 'Mach doch mal Pause.' (why don't you take a break)
en.why: Native speakers use particles all the time. Recognising them stops you trying to translate them word for word.
en.mixup: 'ja' as a particle isn't 'yes'. In 'Das ist ja toll', it just adds surprise.

bs.one: Partikeln su rječce koje dodaju ton, ne sadržaj: doch, mal, ja, denn, eben. Interjektionen su uzvici: ach, oh, au, na ja.
bs.explain: Rječce nikad ne mijenjaju oblik i ne mogu početi rečenicu. Čine njemački prirodnim i ljubaznim. 'Komm mal her' je mekše od 'Komm her'. 'Doch' odgovara 'da' na negativno pitanje: 'Kommst du nicht?' – 'Doch!' (Pa dolazim!).
bs.example: 'Das ist ja interessant!' (pa to je zanimljivo!) 'Mach doch mal Pause.' (de odmori malo)
bs.why: Izvorni govornici ih stalno koriste. Kad ih prepoznaš, nećeš ih pokušavati prevesti riječ po riječ.
bs.mixup: 'ja' kao rječca nije 'da'. U 'Das ist ja toll' samo dodaje iznenađenje.

concepts.youtubeQuery: German sentence structure parts of speech beginner

en.one: A quick method to find the type of any German word in four questions.
en.explain: 1. Capital letter in the middle of a sentence, or der/die/das/ein in front? → Nomen. 2. Does it change with ich/du/er, or end in -en in the dictionary? → Verb. 3. Does it describe a noun and take an ending before it? → Adjektiv. 4. Does it never change? Then it's an Adverb, Präposition (noun follows), Konjunktion (links clauses) or Partikel.
en.example: 'Im Sommer fahren wir oft mit dem Auto ans Meer.' Nouns: Sommer, Auto, Meer. Verb: fahren. Adverb: oft. Prepositions: im, mit, ans. Pronoun: wir.
en.why: This habit turns long, scary sentences into pieces you can understand.
en.mixup: Words can change type: 'das Essen' (the food, noun) and 'essen' (to eat, verb). The capital letter tells you which.

bs.one: Brz metod da odrediš vrstu bilo koje njemačke riječi u četiri pitanja.
bs.explain: 1. Veliko slovo usred rečenice ili der/die/das/ein ispred? → Nomen. 2. Mijenja li se s ich/du/er ili u rječniku završava na -en? → Verb. 3. Opisuje li imenicu i dobija nastavak ispred nje? → Adjektiv. 4. Nikad se ne mijenja? Onda je Adverb, Präposition (iza ide imenica), Konjunktion (spaja rečenice) ili Partikel.
bs.example: 'Im Sommer fahren wir oft mit dem Auto ans Meer.' Imenice: Sommer, Auto, Meer. Glagol: fahren. Prilog: oft. Prijedlozi: im, mit, ans. Zamjenica: wir.
bs.why: Ova navika pretvara duge, strašne rečenice u dijelove koje razumiješ.
bs.mixup: Riječi mogu promijeniti vrstu: 'das Essen' (hrana, imenica) i 'essen' (jesti, glagol). Veliko slovo ti kaže koja je.

q.en: Which article goes with a plural noun?
q.bs: Koji član ide uz imenicu u množini?

explain.en: All plurals use 'die' in the nominative.

Ones first, then tens, written as one word.

q.en: In 'Wir essen um acht', what is 'essen'?
q.bs: U 'Wir essen um acht', šta je 'essen'?

explain.en: Lower case and conjugated with 'wir': a verb.
explain.bs: Malim slovom i konjugiran uz 'wir': glagol.
